evidence_quotes.agenda: Never asked — the call moved straight from callback context into logistics/inventory questions
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: "That's a big number that's like twice what we were seeing in the email estimate... hopefully we can talk about some ways to get that down" — rep gave one round of factors that lower cost (self-pack, remove items) but didn't dig further into what specifically felt high or what the customer was expecting
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: "If this change[s], at the end of the day you only pay for how long it's gonna take" (window) + "we only charge in fifteen minute intervals" (beats-it-pay-less) + "anything you believe you will pack yourself... just let us know" (self-prep tip) — three of five lines present

top_strength: Handled a long, detail-heavy inventory (taxidermy horns, oversized art, a media cabinet, storage-unit logistics) with patience and genuine problem-solving, including proactively offering to check on blanket-rental pricing.
coaching_note: The price-shock moment ("twice what we were seeing in the email estimate") got acknowledged but not dug into two layers deep, and the call ended without a rate-lock or explicit booking ask — both should close out even when a walkthrough is still pending.
